text:
The point P (a, b) undergoes the following three transformations successively :

(a) reflection about the line y = x.

(b) translation through 2 units along the positive direction of x-axis.

(c) rotation through angle $\frac{π}{4}$ about the origin in the anti-clockwise direction.

If the co-ordinates of the final position of the point P are $\left (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},\frac{7}{\sqrt{2}}\right )$, then the value of 2a + b is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Image of A(a, b) along y = x is B(b, a). Translating it 2 units it becomes C(b + 2, a).

Now, applying rotation theorem

$-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{7}{\sqrt{2}}i=((b+2)+ai)\left (\cos \frac{π}{4}+i\sin \frac{π}{4}\right )$

$-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{7}{\sqrt{2}}i=\left (\frac{b+2}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}\right )+i\left (\frac{b+2}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ b $-$ a + 2 = $-$1 ......(i)

and b + 2 + a = 7 ...... (ii)

$\Rightarrow$ a = 4; b = 1

$\Rightarrow$ 2a + b = 9
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text: A possible value of 'x', for which the ninth term in the expansion of $\left \{3^{\log _{3}\sqrt{25^{x-1}+7}}+3^{\left (-\frac{1}{8}\right )\log _{3}(5^{x-1}+1)}\right \}^{10}$ in the increasing powers of $3^{\left (-\frac{1}{8}\right )\log _{3}(5^{x-1}+1)}$ is equal to 180, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The first term of the binomial is $3^{\log _{3}\sqrt{25^{x-1}+7}}=\sqrt{25^{x-1}+7}$ and the second is $3^{-\frac{1}{8}\log _{3}\left (5^{x-1}+1\right )}=\left (5^{x-1}+1\right )^{-1/8}$.

In increasing powers of the second term, $T_{r+1}={}^{10}C_{r}\left (\sqrt{25^{x-1}+7}\right )^{10-r}\left (5^{x-1}+1\right )^{-r/8}$, so the ninth term ($r=8$) is

$T_{9}={}^{10}C_{8}\left (25^{x-1}+7\right )\left (5^{x-1}+1\right )^{-1}=180$

Since ${}^{10}C_{8}=45$, putting $t=5^{x-1}$ (so $25^{x-1}=t^{2}$):

$\dfrac{t^{2}+7}{t+1}=4\Rightarrow t^{2}-4t+3=0\Rightarrow t=1\text{or}t=3$

$t=1$ gives $5^{x-1}=1$, i.e. $x=1$; $t=3$ gives $x=1+\log _{5}3$, which is not among the options.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text: If $\tan \left (\frac{π}{9}\right ),x,\tan \left (\frac{7π}{18}\right )$ are in arithmetic progression and $\tan \left (\frac{π}{9}\right ),y,\tan \left (\frac{5π}{18}\right )$ are also in arithmetic progression, then $|x-2y|$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\dfrac{π}{9}=20^{\circ }$, $\dfrac{7π}{18}=70^{\circ }$ and $\dfrac{5π}{18}=50^{\circ }$, the two arithmetic progressions give

$2x=\tan 20^{\circ }+\tan 70^{\circ },2y=\tan 20^{\circ }+\tan 50^{\circ }$

so

$x-2y=\dfrac{\tan 70^{\circ }-\tan 20^{\circ }-2\tan 50^{\circ }}{2}$

As $70^{\circ }=20^{\circ }+50^{\circ }$,

$\tan 70^{\circ }=\dfrac{\tan 20^{\circ }+\tan 50^{\circ }}{1-\tan 20^{\circ }\tan 50^{\circ }}\Rightarrow \tan 70^{\circ }-\tan 70^{\circ }\tan 20^{\circ }\tan 50^{\circ }=\tan 20^{\circ }+\tan 50^{\circ }$

Since $\tan 70^{\circ }=\cot 20^{\circ }$, $\tan 70^{\circ }\tan 20^{\circ }=1$, so $\tan 70^{\circ }-\tan 50^{\circ }=\tan 20^{\circ }+\tan 50^{\circ }$, that is, $\tan 70^{\circ }-\tan 20^{\circ }-2\tan 50^{\circ }=0$.

Therefore $x-2y=0$ and $|x-2y|=0$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text:
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential 

equation (x $-$ $x^{3})dy = (y + yx^{2}$ $-$ $3x^{4})dx, x > 2$. If y(3) = 3, then y(4) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(x-x^{3})dy=(y+yx^{2}-3x^{4})dx$

$\Rightarrow xdy-ydx=(yx^{2}-3x^{4})dx+x^{3}dy$

$\Rightarrow \frac{xdy-ydx}{x^{2}}=(ydx+xdy)-3x^{2}dx$

$\Rightarrow d\left (\frac{y}{x}\right )=d(xy)-d(x^{3})$

Integrate

$\Rightarrow \frac{y}{x}=xy-x^{3}+c$

given y(3) = 3

$\Rightarrow \frac{3}{3}=3\times 3-3^{3}+c$

$\Rightarrow c=19$

$\therefore$ $\frac{y}{x}=xy-x^{3}+19$

at $x=4,\frac{y}{4}=4y-64+19$

$15y=4\times 45$

$\Rightarrow y=12$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text:
The value of

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{x}{\sqrt{8 1-\sin x}-\sqrt{8 1+\sin x}}\right )$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{x}{\left [(1-\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{8}}-(1+\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{8}}\right ]}\times \left [\frac{(1-\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{8}}+(1+\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{8}}}{(1-\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{8}}+(1+\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{8}}}\right ]$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{x\left [(1-\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{8}}+(1+\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{8}}\right ]}{\left [(1-\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{4}}-(1+\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{4}}\right ]}\times \left [\frac{(1-\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{4}}+(1+\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{4}}}{(1-\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{4}}+(1+\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{4}}}\right ]$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{x[2][2]}{\left [(1-\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}-(1+\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\right ]}\times \left [\frac{(1-\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}+(1+\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}}{(1-\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}+(1+\sin x)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}}\right ]$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{x[2][2][2]}{[(1-\sin x)-(1+\sin x)]}$

$=\lim _{x\to 0}\left (-\frac{1}{2}\right )(2)(2)(2)$ 

 = -4

$\because$ $\left \{\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1\right \}$

text:
Let $f:[0,\infty )\to [0,3]$ be a function defined by 

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \max \{\sin t:0\leq t\leq x\}, & 0\leq x\leq π \\ 2+\cos x, & x>π \end{array} \right.$

Then which of the following is true?
options: f is continuous everywhere but not differentiable exactly at one point in (0, $\infty$)
f is not continuous exactly at two points in (0, $\infty$)
f is continuous everywhere but not differentiable exactly at two points in (0, $\infty$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $0\leq x\leq π$, the largest value of $\sin t$ on $[0,x]$ is $\sin x$ while $\sin$ is increasing, and equals $1$ once $t=\dfrac{π}{2}$ lies in the interval. So

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \sin x, & 0\leq x\leq \dfrac{π}{2} \\ 1, & \dfrac{π}{2}<x\leq π \\ 2+\cos x, & x>π \end{array} \right.$

At $x=\dfrac{π}{2}$: both pieces give the value $1$, so $f$ is continuous. The left derivative is $\cos \dfrac{π}{2}=0$ and the right derivative is $0$, so $f$ is differentiable there.

At $x=π$: $f(π)=1$ and $\lim _{x\to π^{+}}(2+\cos x)=2-1=1$, so $f$ is continuous. The left derivative is $0$ and the right derivative is $-\sin π=0$, so $f$ is differentiable there.

Each piece is differentiable inside its own interval, so $f$ is differentiable at every point of $(0,\infty )$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text: Let N be the set of natural numbers and a relation R on N be defined by $R=\{(x,y)\in N\times N:x^{3}-3x^{2}y-xy^{2}+3y^{3}=0\}$. Then the relation R is :
options: symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive
reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive
reflexive and symmetric, but not transitive
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{3}-3x^{2}y-xy^{2}+3y^{3}=0$

$\Rightarrow x(x^{2}-y^{2})-3y(x^{2}-y^{2})=0$

$\Rightarrow (x-3y)(x-y)(x+y)=0$

Now, x = y $\forall$(x, y) $\in$N $\times$ N so reflexive but not symmetric & transitive.

See, (3, 1) satisfies but (1, 3) does not. Also (3, 1) & (1, $-$1) satisfies but (3, $-$1) does not.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text: Let f : (a, b) $\to$ R be twice differentiable function such that $f(x)=\int\limits _{a}^{x}g(t)dt$ for a differentiable function g(x). If f(x) = 0 has exactly five distinct roots in (a, b), then g(x)g'(x) = 0 has at least :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\int\limits _{a}^{x}g(t)dt$

$\Rightarrow$ f′(x) = g(x)

$\Rightarrow$ f′'(x) = g'(x)

Given, g(x).g'(x) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ f′(x).f′'(x) = 0

Also given f(x) has exactly 5 roots.

So from Rolle's theorem we can say,

f′(x) has 4 roots and f′'(x) has 3 roots.

$\therefore$ f′(x).f′'(x) = 0 has 4 + 3 = 7 roots.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text: If $\int\limits _{0}^{π}(\sin ^{3}x)e^{-\sin ^{2}x}dx=α-\frac{β}{e}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\sqrt{t}e^{t}dt$, then $α$ + $β$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=2\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\sin ^{3}xe^{-\sin ^{2}x}dx$

$=2\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\sin xe^{-\sin ^{2}x}dx+\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\cos x_{I}\qquad e^{-\sin ^{2}x}(-\sin 2x)_{II}dx=2\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\sin xe^{-\sin ^{2}x}dx+\left [\cos xe^{-\sin ^{2}x}\right ]_{0}^{π/2}+\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\sin xe^{-\sin ^{2}x}dx$

$=3\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\sin xe^{-\sin ^{2}x}dx-1$

$=\frac{3}{2}\int\limits _{-1}^{0}\frac{e^{α}dα}{\sqrt{1+α}}-1$ (Put $-\sin ^{2}x = t)$

$=\frac{3}{2e}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\frac{e^{x}}{\sqrt{x}}dx-1$ (put 1 + $α$ = x)

$=\frac{3}{2e}\int\limits _{0}^{1}e^{x}_{II}\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}_{II}dx-1$

$=2-\frac{3}{e}\int\limits _{0}^{1}e^{x}\sqrt{x}dx$

Hence, $α$ + $β$ = 5
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text: If $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$ and $M = A + A^{2} + A^{3} + ....... + A^{20}$, then the sum of all the elements of the matrix M is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A^{n}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & n & \frac{n^{2}+n}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & n \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

So, required sum

$=20\times 3+2\times \left (\frac{20\times 21}{2}\right )+\sum\limits _{r=1}^{20}\left (\frac{r^{2}+r}{2}\right )$

$=60+420+105+35\times 41=2020$
